mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive due to lower real borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs signals labor market strength, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investor confidence improves.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly above the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding economic demand, which predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return by reducing supply-side bottlenecks.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > +2% in the current month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after trigger, with p-value > 0.05 in a backtest.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0 suggests supply-side easing, which is expected to drive positive S&P 20-day forward returns through reduced deflation risk.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the trigger period (mean difference < 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in residential mortgage applications (HOUST) coinciding with rising FEDFUNDS suggests tightening credit conditions, which predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 2200 AND FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean < 0 but p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a positive S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates continued job growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive (mean ≤ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (implied by PAYEMS) combined with elevated industrial production (INDPRO) indicate robust demand, which precedes positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 135,000 AND INDPRO > 112.0 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5 for 3 months) suggests supply-side easing, which should produce negative S&P 20-day forward returns by raising real interest rates expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean ≥ 0, p > 0.05).
